# GLEM auto-generated features

GLEM (Generalized Linear Evaluation Model, Buro 1998 CG'98) auto-generates
conjunction features over a set of base literals, then fits a linear model
over them. Rust owns the base-literal extraction (mirroring
`extract`'s "Rust owns canonicalisation"); Python generates the conjunctions
and fits the model. See
[`GLEM_FORMAT.md`](../../crates/logistello-eval/GLEM_FORMAT.md) for the `GLX1`
extract / `GLM1` model formats.

## 1. Extract GLEM base-literal positions

`glem-extract` emits the `GLX1` columnar binary the Python `train-glem` tool
consumes.

```bash
cargo run --release -p logistello-cli -- glem-extract \
    --base-features cell64,mobility,corner \
    --source selfplay --games 2000 --seed 42 \
    --output /tmp/glem.glx1
```

| Flag | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--base-features` | Comma list of base-feature families (`cell64`,`mobility`,`corner`); order = the spec id recorded in `GLX1` / `GLM1` | `cell64,mobility,corner` |
| `--source` | `selfplay` (seeded, no external data) or `wthor` | `selfplay` |
| `--wthor-dir` | Directory containing `.wtb` files (required for `--source wthor`) | — |
| `--games` | Number of self-play games / max WTHOR games | `2000` |
| `--seed` | Self-play RNG seed (deterministic) | `42` |
| `--max-empties-skip` | Skip positions with more than this many empty squares | keep all |
| `--output` | Output `GLX1` file (required) | — |

## 2. Generate conjunctions + fit the model

`train-glem` does GLEM feature generation + a B3 linear fit.

```bash
uv run logistello-tools train-glem \
    --positions /tmp/glem.glx1 --output /tmp/glem.glm1 \
    --base-features cell64,mobility,corner \
    --max-order 2 --support-threshold 1e-3 --method gd
```

| Flag | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--positions` | Input `GLX1` extract file | required |
| `--output` | Output `GLM1` model file | required |
| `--base-features` | Comma list of base-feature families; must match the `GLX1` corpus spec | from corpus |
| `--max-order` | Max conjunction order K (§6: 1,2,3,4); 1 = plain linear | — |
| `--support-threshold` | τ_support: min training frequency to keep a generated conjunction (§6: 1e-4 .. 1e-2) | — |
| `--weight-threshold` | τ_weight: prune features whose max |weight| (disc units) is below this; 0 keeps all | `0` |
| `--method` | `gd` = faithful B3 GD-300 + muting; `ridge`/`sgd` = scikit-learn least-squares (§7); `logistic` = optional Logistello-1 path (Objective-5 only) | `gd` |

## 3. Play using the GLEM model

```bash
cargo run --release -p logistello-cli -- play \
    --black engine --white random --depth 4 --seed 42 \
    --glem-model /tmp/glem.glm1
```

`--glem-model` makes the `engine` player use `GlemEval` (auto-generated
conjunction features) as the midgame leaf evaluator instead of `PatternEval`
/ `BasicEval`. It is mutually exclusive with `--eval-weights` (PatternEval vs
GlemEval are alternative leaf evaluators) and composes with `--probcut` /
`--mpc`.

> **Honest notes:** the `cell64` base family at `--max-order 2` can produce a
> very large conjunction space; the generator applies a numerical clamp to
> the cell64-order2 expansion to keep training tractable, which is a
> deliberate approximation noted here. The **Objective-5** apparatus
> compares GLEM auto-features vs the manual `PatternEval` on the same
> held-out corpus (design doc §5):
>
> ```bash
> uv run logistello-tools objective5 \
>     --glx1 /tmp/heldout.glx1 --glm1 /tmp/glem.glm1 \
>     --pex1 /tmp/heldout.pex1 --lgw1 /tmp/w.lgw1
> ```
